subject: SLA validation & MAP: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private benchmarking
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Greene <alyssa@northstar.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21 09:18 -0700
Subject: Proposed MAP and SLAs: benchmarking plan for hosting modes

Hi Alyssa,

Thanks again for the time earlier — excited about the possibility of Redwood powering the inference tier for NorthStar. Per our chat, I attached a first-pass MAP (northstar_map_v1.xlsx) that splits the evaluation into a 2-week technical validation focusing on throughput/latency/TTFT and autoscaling behavior across Hosting modes (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private).

High-level ask: can we validate the following KPIs during the eval?
- P50 / P95 token latency for 3 representative prompt classes (short, medium, long)
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) for streaming endpoints
- Sustained throughput at target concurrency (steady 40 qps, burst to 120 qps)
- Cold vs warm-start behavior (KV cache warm conditions)
- Autoscale response: ramp to sustained load and back; cold-start penalties
- Isolation/predictability: variance under noisy neighbors for Dedicated vs Private

Proposed timeline (in MAP): kickoff 6/28, 10 business days of active tests, decision-target: 7/09. If that looks tight we can extend by a week.

I put a few specific measurement notes in the spreadsheet but next steps would be:
1) Confirm the KPI targets you care about (I included suggested targets in the sheet)
2) Approve test windows and provide SRE access (or we can run from Redwood side)
3) Confirm which deployment modes you want instrumented (Hosted + Dedicated + Private = recommended)

I cc'd Karthik and Monica from our team for test plan and infra details.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a more detailed runbook if you confirm the above.

Best,
Rishi
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks for the doc and the clear checklist. A few immediate questions from our infra/ML infra team:

- Are the metrics you collect agent-side (Redwood dashboards) or do we need to run our own telemetry? We prefer independent measurement if possible.
- For the Private deployment we have strict VPC peering and egress controls; we’ll need a security checklist before any access.

Targets we want to validate (initial ask): p50 < 90ms, p95 < 420ms for short prompts; TTFT < 60ms; steady concurrency 40, burst 120.

Procurement: please send any master terms and the MAP as an SOW so we can attach to the PO.

Alyssa —

Great — thanks for the targets, that’s exactly the specificity we need. Per your questions, I attached a short runbook (latency_runbook.pdf) and the harness config (benchmark_harness_config.yaml). Quick answers inline below:

- Test harness: Redwood will run the harness from an isolated customer namespace for Hosted and Dedicated; for Private we provide a small orchestrator VM inside your VPC and remote agents will be disabled. The harness config shows instance profiles and the request distribution we’ll use.
- Metrics: we will stream telemetry to your Drive with independent logs for p50/p95/TTFT. Redwood will also publish its dashboard for correlation; we recommend you collect a parallel Prometheus scrape for independent validation.
- Dedicated config: default test cluster = 4x A100-40GB (NVIDIA) with our optimized kernel stack; we’ll tune batch sizes per prompt class.
- Private: we included a short network & KMS checklist in the runbook; onboarding typically takes 48–72 hours once we have network access.

Important test parameters (defined in the runbook):
- Prompt mix: 60% short (<64 tokens), 30% medium (64–256), 10% long (>256)
- Concurrency profile: steady 40 qps for 30m intervals, 5x burst to 120 qps for 2m every 15m
- KV cache: measure cold-start (empty) vs warmed (10 preceding tokens cached)
- Autoscale: measure time to add capacity at sustained burst start and cooldown time after burst
- Isolation test: on Dedicated we’ll inject noisy background batch jobs to measure tail variance

If that looks good I’ll send an updated MAP with the timeline and DocuSign link for signature.

Thanks — Karthik and Monica, wanted you to see the harness config and confirm infra sizing/ops readiness.

Rishi
Attachment: latency_runbook.pdf, benchmark_harness_config.yaml
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-06-23 09:14 -0700
Subject: Internal: infra sizing and isolation notes for NSA MAP

Rishi / Monica —

Notes from infra side before we send the finalized MAP:
- Dedicated cluster: 4x A100-40GB with 32 CPU and 256GB RAM management host is our baseline. Expect sustained token throughput ~1.2M tokens/min with batching tuned for short prompts.
- Network: place Dedicated in a private subnet with pinned egress through our peering connection; for Private, expect 1–2ms additional network latency depending on your VPC egress path.
- Isolation: Dedicated provides tenant-level isolation; for extreme tail-protection use the private option or add reserved capacity (we suggested reserve blocks in the MAP).
- Autoscale behavior: our autoscaler scales in ~90–120s under a sustained ramp to the sizes above; cold-starts for model containers are ~8–12s if no cache present.

I’ll prepare a short ops runbook snippet to include in northstar_map_v2.xlsx addressing required IAM roles, KMS scopes, and sample Prometheus metrics to capture.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Please sign the MAP (DocuSign) and confirm whether Redwood runs the harness from our side (recommended) or you will run independent scrapes.

Best,
Rishi
